thread:
emily.c: Hi folks 1 1 Im starting the adoption process and expecting placement in late Aug. A few quick things Im trying to line up: 1) Are adoptive parents eligible for Redwoods parental leave top-up and childcare stipend? 2) I may need to travel abroad for the finalization week 1 does that affect benefits or payroll? 3) Can we get a short-term contractor approved to cover my recruiting tasks for ~8 weeks?
people-ops: Congrats, Emily! :tada: Short answers: 1) Yes, adoptive parents are eligible for the same parental leave policy and top-up provided you submit the formal placement/legal docs. Childcare stipend (monthly reimbursement) is available if you opt in on the benefits form.
people-ops: 2) International travel generally doesnt affect pay or eligibility, but we do need the placement paperwork and a signed leave request before travel. Also, if youre outside the U.S. for >30 days we need to flag payroll/benefits to confirm tax withholding implications. If you plan that, CC benefits@redwood.com and well loop Payroll and Legal.
payroll-bot: Note: to ensure top-up processes on schedule, upload placement docs to https://benefits.redwood.com/leave-forms and tag as "Placement docs" at least one full pay period before your first paid leave day. Missing docs = top-up delayed by one payroll.
sarah-legal: If youre travelling internationally for placement, bring copies of adoption paperwork and check entry requirements. From a Redwood perspective we need the court/country adoption certificate or placement letter to finalize parental pay. If travel crosses any export-controlled equipment rules (laptop with restricted data), coordinate with InfoSec before you depart.
emily.c: Thanks 1 for the heads up on >30 days tax flag. Im planning a 10-day trip, so should be fine. For the contractor: whats the fastest path to get someone in for 8 weeks to cover recruiting ops?
hiring-ops: Easiest is to request a contractor headcount pull via the internal hiring intake form: https://hr.redwood.com/hiring-intake -> choose "temporary contractor" and tag me. Include scope (sourcing + screens + offer coordination), weekly hours, and expected rate. We can fast-track approvals for parental leave coverage.
daniel.p: I can be backup on offer discussions; happy to take the final call if needed. Emily, can you add a short hiring checklist in the req so we know the priority roles?
emily.c: Will do. Last Q: can I preserve PTO to use after leave or must I use it concurrently? Id prefer to save PTO to extend time at home.
people-ops: You can elect to reserve PTO. When you fill the internal leave form, choose "Reserve PTO" and payroll will not disburse PTO concurrently. If you want to use PTO to reach full salary during initial weeks, indicate that instead. Well confirm in writing on the approval.
payroll-bot: Reminder: medical benefits continue during paid parental leave. If youre on Redwood insurance and travel internationally, check in with benefits@redwood.com for provider network and out-of-pocket rules.
sarah-legal: One last note: adoption placements sometimes have confidentiality timelines. If any paperwork is sealed, you can provide HR with a redacted placement letter plus a statement from your attorney confirming placement date. Thats sufficient for payroll processing.
emily.c: Amazing, thank you all. Ill submit the intake form for the contractor now and upload a redacted placement letter once I have it. Appreciate the quick responses :heart:
